modifications: Stream CSV rows directly through pigz -5 without writing an intermediate plain CSV.
Validate bar fields and ordering, verify the compressed SHA-256, and publish compact manifests atomically.
Separate the internal pipeline version from the manifest schema version.
Reprocess matching cached gzip data in memory when its pipeline version differs, using randomized same-directory temporary files.
Use the fixed US market calendar to require complete daily session coverage.
Record session and calendar digests plus stat metadata, diagnose missing sessions, and redownload incomplete data.
Require and validate an ordered pipeline version changelog whose entries exactly match every pipeline version through the current version.
Treat an orphaned gzip or manifest as cache corruption requiring --repair, while reserving --force for deliberate refreshes of coherent cache entries.
Strengthen end-of-day validation with New York session-midnight timestamps, complete OHLC/VWAP bounds, positive activity, and trade-count versus volume checks.
Separate immutable Alpaca download ownership from pricing/data validation ownership.
Preserve every downloaded row and atomically maintain one symbol-level integrity manifest with exact failed rows, validation errors, and dataset coverage failures.
Authenticate the frozen gzip against its download manifest before every local validation or forced replacement.
Abort on a download SHA-256 mismatch without publishing pricing/data integrity or making the data eligible for repair.
Separate pipeline processing receipts from integrity failures.
Record every processed download SHA and pipeline version in pipeline.manifest.json while publishing only actual failures to integrity_failure.manifest.json.
Keep an incoming response in memory until all row and dataset integrity checks finish, and only then begin streaming unchanged rows through pigz.
Keep the failure-only manifest present with the pipeline version even when its failures array is empty, and never mix findings from different pipeline versions.
Store the pipeline version once at pipeline-manifest scope and keep individual receipts limited to downloaded-artifact identity and processing metadata.
Close the pigz stderr pipe on both successful completion and exceptional process cleanup.
Use self-describing internal names and explicit ownership terminology without changing downloaded filenames, manifest filenames, or serialized keys.
